\chapter{Boolean Analysis — General}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.Products.General
\section{Overview}
Coordinate hypercontractivity tensorizes on heterogeneous finite probability products. Both conjugate hypercontractive estimates are obtained at the sharp discrete radius and at the minimum-atom radius.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Tensorization above the first moment]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity_induction_gt_one}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.expect, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.mass, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise_kernel, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteTensorization.norm_tensorization}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $p\ge1$, $q>1$, and $0\le\rho\le1$. If every coordinate probability law satisfies $\|\rho g+(1-\rho)\mathbb E_i g\|_{q,i}\le\|g\|_{p,i}$ for every real $g$ on that coordinate, then $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{p,P}$ for every $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$; $\|g\|_{p,i}=(\sum_{a\in\Omega_i}w_i(a)|g(a)|^p)^{1/p}$ and $\mathbb E_i g=\sum_{a\in\Omega_i}w_i(a)g(a)$, where $w_i$ gives the probability masses in coordinate $i$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Removing squared moment bounds]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rpow_norm_le_of_sq_moments}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every $A,B\ge0$ and $p,q\in\mathbb R$, the inequality $A^{2/q}\le B^{2/p}$ implies $A^{1/q}\le B^{1/p}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Monotonicity of quadratic noise]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finite_noise_quadratic_mono}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
Let $I$ be a finite set with nonnegative weights $w_i$ satisfying $\sum_iw_i=1$, and let $g:I\to\mathbb R$ and $0\le\rho\le\sigma$. Then $\rho^2\sum_iw_ig_i^2+(1-\rho^2)(\sum_iw_ig_i)^2\le\sigma^2\sum_iw_ig_i^2+(1-\sigma^2)(\sum_iw_ig_i)^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp coordinate hypercontractivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finite_coordinate_hypercontractivity_sharp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_duality, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_identities, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.finite_noise_sharp_contraction, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finite_noise_quadratic_mono, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.rpow_norm_le_of_sq_moments, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sharpDiscreteRadius}
\difficulty{5}
Let $I$ be finite with weights $w_i\ge\lambda$, $\sum_iw_i=1$, $0<\lambda<1/2$, and $q>2$. Put $r=\sqrt{\sinh(\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)/q)/\sinh(\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)/(q/(q-1)))}$. For $0\le\rho\le r$, the operator $Ng=\rho g+(1-\rho)\sum_iw_ig_i$ satisfies $\|Ng\|_{q,w}\le\|g\|_{2,w}$ and $\|Ng\|_{2,w}\le\|g\|_{q/(q-1),w}$. Here $\|h\|_{p,w}=(\sum_{i\in I}w_i|h_i|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sharp product hypercontractivity]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity_sharp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.SharpDiscrete.radius_pos_lt_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.finite_coordinate_hypercontractivity_sharp, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity_induction_gt_one, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sharpDiscreteRadius}
\difficulty{4}
Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$ with every coordinate atom at least $\lambda$, where $0<\lambda<1/2$, and let $q>2$. Put $r=\sqrt{\sinh(\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)/q)/\sinh(\log((1-\lambda)/\lambda)/(q/(q-1)))}$. For $0\le\rho\le r$ and every $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$, $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{2,P}$ and $\|T_\rho f\|_{2,P}\le\|f\|_{q/(q-1),P}$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $T_a h=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}a^{|S|}h_S$ for every real rate $a$; $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$. The powers indexed by subset cardinalities are natural powers, including $0^0=1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hyperbolic sine ratio bound]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sinh_ratio_lower_bound}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $a,b$ be real numbers with $0<a\le b$. Then $(a/b)e^{a-b}\le\sinh(a)/\sinh(b)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Minimum-atom radius comparison]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.coarse_radius_le_sharp}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sharpDiscreteRadius, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.sinh_ratio_lower_bound}
\difficulty{5}
Let $q>2$ and $0<\lambda<1$. For $r_q(t)=\sqrt{\sinh(\log((1-t)/t)/q)/\sinh(\log((1-t)/t)/(q/(q-1)))}$, one has $\lambda^{1/2-1/q}/\sqrt{q-1}\le r_q(\lambda/(1+\lambda))$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Hypercontractive finite probability law]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.one_coordinate_hypercontractivity}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.AtomBound, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.Point, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.noise, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.FiniteProduct.norm, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.product_hypercontractivity}
\difficulty{1}
Let $P$ be a probability law on a finite outcome space $\Omega$, with every atom of mass at least $\lambda>0$, where $0<\lambda\le1$, and let $q>2$. For $0\le\rho\le\lambda^{1/2-1/q}/\sqrt{q-1}$, the operator $T_\rho f=\rho f+(1-\rho)\mathbb E_Pf$ satisfies $\|T_\rho f\|_{q,P}\le\|f\|_{2,P}$ and $\|T_\rho f\|_{2,P}\le\|f\|_{q/(q-1),P}$ for every real $f$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $\|h\|_{p,P}=(\mathbb E_P|h|^p)^{1/p}$ for $p>0$.
\end{theorem}
